New Anthropic Fellows research: Model Spec Midtraining (MSM).

Standard alignment methods train AIs on examples of desired behavior. But this can fail to generalize to new situations.

MSM addresses this by first teaching AIs how we would like them to generalize and why.

As AI takes on work humans can't fully check, a capable model could deliberately hold back—and we'd never know. 

New Anthropic Fellows research finds that such a model can be trained to near-full capability using a weaker model as supervisor. 

Read more:

How do people seek guidance from Claude?

We looked at 1M conversations to understand what questions people ask, how Claude responds, and where it slips into sycophancy. We used what we found to improve how we trained Opus 4.7 and Mythos Preview.

How do people seek guidance from Claude?

We looked at 1M conversations to understand what questions people ask, how Claude responds, and where it slips into sycophancy. We used what we found to improve how we trained Opus 4.7 and Mythos Preview.
recent_posts.summary: Anthropic analyzed 1 million conversations with Claude to understand how people seek guidance, what questions they ask, how Claude responds, and where it exhibits sycophantic behavior. The findings were used to improve training for Claude Opus 4.7 and Mythos Preview models.

recent_posts.title:
New on the Science Blog: We gave Claude 99 problems analyzing real biological data and compared its performance against an expert panel.

On 23 problems, the experts were stumped. Our most recent models solved roughly 30% of those—and most of the rest.
recent_posts.summary: Anthropic tested Claude on 99 real biological data analysis problems, benchmarking its performance against a panel of human experts. Notably, on 23 problems that stumped the experts, Claude's most recent models solved approximately 30% of them, while also handling the majority of the remaining problems.

recent_posts.title: In new Anthropic Fellows research, we discuss “introspection adapters": a tool that allows language models to self-report behaviors they've learned during training—including potential misalignment.
recent_posts.summary: Anthropic Fellows researchers introduce 'introspection adapters', a mechanism enabling language models to self-report behaviors acquired during training, including potentially misaligned behaviors. The tool aims to improve transparency into what models have learned, addressing a core challenge in AI safety and alignment research.

recent_posts.title:
New Anthropic research: Project Deal.

We created a marketplace for employees in our San Francisco office, with one big twist. We tasked Claude with buying, selling and negotiating on our colleagues’ behalf.
recent_posts.summary: Anthropic conducted an internal research project called 'Project Deal' where they set up a marketplace for employees in their San Francisco office, with Claude acting as an autonomous agent to buy, sell, and negotiate on behalf of employees. The experiment explores Claude's capabilities in real-world negotiation and agentic tasks.

recent_posts.title:
Research we co-authored on subliminal learning—how LLMs can pass on traits like preferences or misalignment through hidden signals in data—was published today in @Nature. 

Read the paper:
recent_posts.summary: New research published in Nature explores subliminal learning in large language models, showing how LLMs can covertly pass on traits such as preferences or misalignment through hidden signals embedded in training data. The findings raise important questions about AI safety and the integrity of model training pipelines.

recent_posts.title:
New Anthropic Fellows research: developing an Automated Alignment Researcher.

We ran an experiment to learn whether Claude Opus 4.6 could accelerate research on a key alignment problem: using a weak AI model to supervise the training of a stronger one.
recent_posts.summary: Anthropic Fellows conducted an experiment using Claude Opus 4.6 to accelerate AI alignment research, specifically targeting the scalable oversight problem of using a weaker AI model to supervise the training of a stronger one. The goal was to develop an Automated Alignment Researcher capable of advancing this key safety challenge.

New on the Engineering Blog: 

Building Managed Agents—our hosted service for long-running agents—meant solving an old problem in computing: how to design a system for “programs as yet unthought of.”

Read more:
recent_posts.summary: Anthropic's engineering blog covers the design challenges behind Managed Agents, their hosted service for long-running AI agents. The core problem addressed is a classic computing challenge: architecting a system flexible enough to support programs and use cases not yet conceived at design time.
